title: One attempt's adoption confirmation let item 21 end a refreshed credential's previous version, although the attempts of a run share its credential, so another active attempt could lose its secret
resolution: A version ends only once every attempt of the run that held it adopted it or a later one or let go of its ownership, decided serialized per run (contract page section 6, scenario Second attempt still holds the previous version); a contract text check failed before; item 21 tests behavior

title: The eleven new observations carried no recovery epoch, so an observation from before a restore could change the restored timeline or credential state, against the rule of launch authorization section 7
resolution: Every new observation payload requires recoveryEpoch, and one of another epoch or received in quarantine is kept as evidence only (contract page section 9, requirement Session observation recovery epoch); tests that failed before cover all eleven

title: Every port refusal of a turn delivery left the turn queued for the next generation, although the port's conflict for a seen turn ID proves acceptance, so the turn could be refused again and again
resolution: Architect's answer of 2026-10-28: port-refused only for refusals proving non-acceptance, a new session.turn.acceptance-unknown (conflict, timeout, crash), and a timeline operation making the turn outcome-unknown, never resent (contract page section 3, session timeline 4.4); tests failed before

title: The request recorded observation dropped the port's classified operation, so the control plane could not check a push-to-task-branch standing rule against the task branch
resolution: RequestRecordedPayload carries an optional ClassifiedOperation, a push with its full branch ref, only for a permission request, and a rule matches only a push to the task branch in the use transaction (contract page section 9, requirement Classified permission request); tests that failed before

title: A delegation result for a request no longer open went to a host turn, which included answered requests that the session timeline admits only as a repeat
resolution: Only an expired or unresolved request takes the host turn; a result for an answered request, delivery-uncertain included, is a repeat that sends nothing (contract page section 5, spec delta scenario Result for an answered request); text only, no schema change

title: The delegation result command was due only when a child task ended, so a delegation that requestDelegation rejected left the parent request without its rejected result
resolution: The command is due when the delegation result becomes ended, a rejected delegation included (contract page sections 3 and 5, spec delta scenario Rejected delegation); text only, no schema change

title: The terminal refusal reasons had no typed answer for a terminal whose program or pseudo-terminal failed to start after the open's checks passed
resolution: TerminalRefusalReason gains terminal-start-failed, with no error text, mapped to relay.terminal.refused, terminal.ended with reason refused, and the close terminal-ended (contract page section 8, requirement Terminal start failure); tests that failed before

title: A turn whose acceptance is unknown could still run in the harness while the next queued turn of the same generation was sent, so its requests and output were refused and one turn at a time broke
resolution: Architect's amendment of 2026-10-28: the host stops a still running generation before it reports acceptance unknown, no later turn is delivered in it, and a refusal naming the submitted turn as runningTurnId reports it delivered; port section 6, timeline 4.2 and 4.4; tests failed before

title: An observation that the session timeline refused for another reason than a repeat had no defined handling, so the producer's sequence could stall or the observation vanish
resolution: Such an observation is applied without effect: confirmed, recorded in the inbox and cursor, and logged as evidence, as observation-consumption treats stale and other-epoch observations (contract page section 9, requirement Observations the timeline refuses); text only

title: A turn refused with port-refused stays queued with no rule that ends its generation, and a permanent invalid refusal would block every later turn of the session
resolution: Architect answer (b): not-found, unavailable, and precondition-failed naming another running turn or none stop the generation, the turn stays queued; the plugin's invalid is reported as turn-invalid and recordTurnRefused makes the turn refused, final, so later turns proceed

title: The page counted every invalid as proof of non-acceptance, although the host parser's invalid for a malformed result and a throwing plugin prove nothing, and the schema did not describe the crash reason
resolution: Only an invalid the plugin returned is port-refused; the host parser's invalid and a throw are crash, and the reason description names the plugin internal failure and the restart with a journaled command without outcome (port section 2 rules 2 and 3)

title: A spec delta scenario still counted eleven session and adoption observations after the acceptance unknown observation made them twelve
resolution: The scenario says twelve; a structural count of the messages that require SessionProtocolVersion gives 4 commands and 12 observations

title: The reattach cursor after was not bound to a terminal, so a cursor of an ended terminal skipped the first output chunks of the new one, and an after beyond the last sequence was undefined
resolution: terminal.attach requires terminalId with after, after applies only to that terminal, otherwise output follows from the earliest retained chunk, and an after beyond the last sequence closes with invalid-frame; a test that failed before

title: The session binding cited G3 plan rows 18 and 19 for the model and effort, which those rows do not mention, and named an item 19 obligation without its source
resolution: The page and design cite ADR 0014 and the architect's answer; the item 18 and 19 obligation now cites the G3 plan's ADR 0014 obligation row (docs/g3-plan.md:187 on dev) and docs/contracts/agent-harness-port.md:89, as the architect answered

title: The author self-check still counted 11 new observations after the acceptance unknown observation made them 12
resolution: The self-check counts 12 observations and notes that the twelfth came with 3b6bb234

title: The design's recovery epoch fix said that 11 new observations require the epoch, although 12 do since 3b6bb234
resolution: The design says all 12, the twelfth since 3b6bb234

title: The 503 answer of openWorkerRelay was copied from openTerminal and named a closed relay connection, which cannot apply to the relay's own upgrade
resolution: The 503 answer names only an unavailable store

title: The NATS schema table test comment named items 13 and 18 for the session messages of the adapter tables, which design decision 1 and the contract page give to item 13 alone
resolution: The comment names item 13

title: The NATS schema table test found session work by searching schema text for SessionProtocolVersion, so a description naming it would silently drop a version 1 message from coverage
resolution: The test reads the protocolVersion references of the payload and the observation metadata structurally

title: Revoking the operator bearer did not close an open terminal connection, although the terminal takes interactive input
resolution: The connection closes with unauthenticated when its operator bearer is revoked, as the relay closes when the worker credential is revoked (contract page section 7, close table, requirement Terminal connection end)

title: A cookie-authenticated terminal upgrade without an Origin header had no defined answer
resolution: A cookie upgrade without Origin is refused with 403 csrf-token-invalid like a foreign origin

title: The upgrades required Sec-WebSocket-Protocol to equal one value, so a client that offers a list of subprotocols, as RFC 6455 allows, would get 400
resolution: Both upgrades accept a comma-separated list that offers their protocol, and the 101 answer selects it; a test that failed before

title: The contract did not say how pseudo-terminal bytes, including invalid UTF-8 and split multibyte sequences, become JSON text output
resolution: The worker decodes the bytes as streaming UTF-8, carries a split sequence into the next chunk, and replaces each invalid sequence with U+FFFD

title: The run-wide adoption rule was checked by a pattern over a schema description, while the pass 1 record called it a test that failed before without saying it checks only text
resolution: The pass 1 record now calls it a check of the contract text, and item 21 owns the behavioral test (contract page section 12)

title: A restart that finds a turn delivery journaled without its outcome reports crash even when submitTurn was never called, so the turn is lost needlessly
resolution: The architect's binding answer on pass 1 finding 3, restated on 2026-10-28, names this restart case crash; narrowing it by a journaled submission intent would reopen that decision

title: The record lists make verify logs 1 to 5, 7, and 8, with no log 6 and no word on it
resolution: The revision says that no log numbered 6 exists and that the numbering skipped it

title: The record gave the second re-route a fix of a verify run as its reason, although the binding was new implementation before pass 1
resolution: The revision records the reason: the implementation was not complete before pass 1, so the routed diff changed and worker step 4 required a new route
